answer: A trading haven should admit agents only after they post a ridge bond that rises with the privileges they claim, so creating many identities becomes expensive rather than free. Admission alone is not enough: the haven runs unannounced gale audits, sudden bursts of distinct, verifiable work that each identity must complete within a short window, with results checked against public records. One operator cannot plausibly finish dozens of different jobs at once, so Sybil clusters stall, miss deadlines, and lose their bonds, while genuine agents pass routinely and keep trading.
